alternatives.label: Population health, behaviour and social policy
alternatives.concept: A programme connecting epidemiology and prevention with health psychology, lifespan development, biological disease mechanisms, social inequalities and environmental justice. Quantitative, qualitative and evidence-synthesis methods support inquiry, while public economics, organisational psychology and policy analysis examine collective responses. It does not reproduce the Dutch healthcare curriculum or the final supervised placement and thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual epidemiological, health-behaviour, lifespan, inequality and policy contributions sustain the title; no clinical or full Health Sciences qualification is implied.
progression: Formal earlier prerequisites and covered offerings checked; statistics precede advanced methods, gateways precede biological/health dependents, PPD is in year one.

candidates.label: Privacy and protection of health-app data
candidates.reason: AI Ethics actually addresses privacy, fairness, responsibility and clinical/psychological applications. The health-methods and ethical courses add evidence appraisal and moral reasoning. This does not establish a sustained distinct24-course health-data protection/informatics programme with further specialised data-governance or medical-information-system teaching. A different context for one ethics course is insufficient; the taught privacy contribution is acknowledged.

selection.assessment: One substantive population-health/behaviour/policy programme passes for the confirmed core. Hospital organisation is addressed through specific policy, economics and organisational contributions, with Dutch care-system gaps explicit; those actual contributions do not supply additional specialist healthcare-management progression for a distinct full alternative. Health-app privacy is separately tested and lacks sustained specialist content. Career/illustrative rows do not generate programmes.

blocks: Behaviour and health across the lifespan
Both address development and health across early life. UCR treats the whole lifespan rather than supplying a dedicated childhood public-health course.
Both study psychological aspects of health behaviour and change. UCR adds biopsychosocial illness, stress and treatment decisions; it does not reproduce the complete VU lifestyle intervention course.

Both develop descriptive empirical inquiry and analysis. UCR supplies design, measurement and descriptive/inferential statistics in a broader social-science setting; this is not an identical health-methods sequence.
Both include exploratory qualitative inquiry; UCR teaches interviews, coding and reflexive interpretation without certifying the same health-specific syllabus.

notes.text: UCR offers broader population-health, behavioural and policy inquiry. It provides less dedicated Dutch/international healthcare organisation and implementation research, and does not reproduce the VU supervised placement, professional-development sequence or required health-science thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Health Sciences examines population health and wellbeing through biological, behavioural, social and policy perspectives. The confirmed early curriculum studies health inequalities, lifestyle and environment, health systems, prevention and health across the lifespan.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed population-health, behavioural, lifespan and research-methods core supports a meaningful broader UCR programme in population health, behaviour and social policy; the unverified final-year research/professional culmination is outside this comparison. UCR supplies actual epidemiological, health-psychological and empirical inquiry with biological and policy complements. Dedicated care-system and implementation depth differs; the final VU research placement and required endwork are not reproduced.

curriculum.limitation: The nominal VU degree is 180 EC. The displayed 150 EC comprise the confirmed first two years and at least 30 EC of minor/elective study. The revised-cohort allocation of the final 30 EC, including later methods, professional development, research placement and thesis, is not verified.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic-core comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: Confirmed 120 EC in the first two years, including two separately restricted 6 EC choices, plus at least 30 EC of approved minor/elective study:150 documentedEC.
comparisonScope.excluded: The revised-cohort final 30 EC allocation and progression, including Methodology 5, professional development, placement, thesis and their dependent culmination. No complete external pathway or placement eligibility is certified.

acceptance.claim: The confirmed population-health, behavioural, lifespan and research-methods core supports a meaningful broader UCR programme in population health, behaviour and social policy; the unverified final-year research/professional culmination is outside this comparison.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Final30EC primarily comprise advanced applied methods and an18EC or differently weighted supervised research placement/endwork.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Full research training and culminating practice may differ substantially. The independently specified120EC population-health/behaviour/methods core and the broader UCR response remain; no final-year research equivalence is claimed.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The final30EC combine revised Methodology5, professional development, more implementation/organisation or a differently weighted thesis/placement.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: This changes specialist culmination/progression and possibly preparation. All such dependent full-pathway claims are excluded; confirmed early health determinants, lifespan and methods inquiry and the UCR response survive.
